document.title: Afghanistan: Jalaluddin Haqqani's Emergence As a Key Taliban Commander (Islamabad 00154)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Haqqani History: Bin Ladin's Advocate Inside the Taliban
document.note: [Confidential] Haqqani is reported to be more liberal on social policy such as women's rights than other Taliban officials, but unable to influence Taliban positions. He remains a respected, competent and influential officer in Taliban military affairs. His ties to various radical Arab groups concern the Department of State; one source says that in exchange for weapons and money he offers shelter to Arabs in Paktia province.

persons.name: Jalaluddin Haqqani
persons.role: Taliban 'Acting Minister of Tribes and Borders'; reported commander of Taliban forces north of Kabul
persons.status_detail: aged 50 in Jan 1997; studied sixteen years in Afghan and Pakistani madrassahs

mentions.quote: FORMER AFGHAN RESISTANCE COMMANDER JALALUDDIN HAQQANI MAY NOW BE IN CHARGE OF THE TALIBAN'S FORCES NORTH OF KABUL
HAQQANI, 50, HAS BEEN A COMMANDER FOR THE TALIBAN SINCE THE GROUP'S BEGINNING IN 1994.
IN EXCHANGE FOR WEAPONS AND MONEY, HAQQANI IS "OFFERING SHELTER FOR VARIOUS ARABS IN AREAS OF PAKTIA PROVINCE."

persons.name: Mullah Borjan

events.description: Taliban begin; Haqqani commander for Taliban since start.
Taliban defeat Hekmatyar forces in eastern Afghanistan; Haqqani reportedly key.
Taliban seize Kabul.
Mullah Borjan killed near Kabul.
Mullah Ghaus dismissive of Haqqani in meeting with US DCM.
Abdul Wahab speaks to US Poloff.
Payenda speaks to Poloff.
Cable sent.
Mullah Borjan, Taliban chief military commander, killed near Kabul.
Taliban founded; Haqqani a commander from the beginning.
Taliban, aided by Haqqani, defeat Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami forces in eastern Afghanistan (Aug-Sept 1996).
Abdul Wahab speaks with the Embassy political officer about Haqqani.
Mullah Ghaus meets the US DCM and is dismissive of Haqqani.
General Payenda briefs the Embassy political officer on Haqqani.
A Taliban supporter tells the political officer Haqqani has links with Arab radicals.
Taliban select Abdul Razaq as governor of Herat.
Embassy Islamabad cable on Haqqani's emergence as a key Taliban commander north of Kabul.
A Taliban supporter told the Embassy political officer that Haqqani has links with Islamic extremists and radical Arab groups.
Mullah Ghaus met the DCM and was dismissive of Haqqani's role in the Taliban hierarchy.
General Payenda told the Embassy political officer that the Supreme Defense Council sees Haqqani's rise as part of a Taliban 'hard men' policy.
Taliban recently selected Abdul Razaq as governor of Herat.
Embassy Islamabad cable assessing that Haqqani's forces north of Kabul add to Taliban military clout, though he has little influence in Taliban circles.

key_claims: Haqqani may now lead Taliban forces north of Kabul, replacing Mullah Borjan, though the Taliban have not confirmed it.
Observers see Haqqani as influential on military matters but not on Taliban political or social policy.
A Taliban supporter claimed Haqqani shelters Arabs in Paktia in exchange for weapons and money.
Taliban officials like Ghaus oppose Haqqani's extremist ties and downplay his importance.
Dostam's representative saw Haqqani's rise as a Taliban policy of placing 'hard men' in key military posts.
Haqqani's Zadran forces are seen as undisciplined and likely to develop tensions with the Taliban.
